title: Add makima interpolation and refactor animation key retrieving partially
body:
- Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57952
- Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86003

This PR adds [Modified Akima interpolation](https://blogs.mathworks.com/cleve/2019/04/29/makima-piecewise-cubic-interpolation/) (a.k.a. makima interpolation).

While cubic interpolation considers 4 consecutive keys, makima interpolation considers 6 keys. As I mentioned in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/57954, we should refactor the method of key retrieving. This PR refactor especially looped keys regardless of the number of keys, so this is last step to solve https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57952, as follow up https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/57954 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/70547. I've split the commits to make the review easier, but I can squash them after the review if keeping them separate is not necessary.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07199d52-f147-4e2e-b752-be87bf7f41f7

**Demo project:**
[makima.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32666870/makima.zip) (Partial quote/reuse from https://github.com/fire-archive/godot-40592/tree/main/tests/cubic_slerp)

So, compared to cubic interpolation, makima is less prone to overshoot when intervals are short, and overshooting can be completely prevented by setting 3 consecutive keys to the same value. This is documented, and in the case of #86003, placing some keys at the edges with narrow segment can prevent overshooting.

**1 key in the start position:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b4ad15c-00a9-486a-85d8-b70bfc0eae05

Due to the characteristics of Akima, it looks ahead at more keys than cubic, so the initial horizontal movement path wobbles a bit.

**2 keys in the start position:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52278d7a-0880-4023-a5e9-23b188341811

Overshoot occurs, just like with cubic.

**3 keys in the start position:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e983c33e-4402-42eb-89db-b86e8fca3f08

Now it is stable, unlike the cubic overshoot.

For Quaternions, we will reuse the implementation from #63593. Regarding error cancellation, as done there, the result is computed in both the "from" and "to" spaces and blended to cancel the error.

Makima references keys further away than cubic, so the rotation to those keys can cross the singularity of the `log()` conversion (at ±360 deg), where `log()` no longer keeps the expmap continuous with the neighboring keys. I added a helper that makes the expmap from a wider range[^1] (by shifting the `log()` result by ±720 deg) and picks the point on the expmap closest to the neighboring key.

[^1]: The expmap is derived from axis and angle (a rotation vector whose length is the angle), so it is not limited to ±360 deg

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fe944e6-2b4b-4704-be74-217d5f246dc7

Makima is easier to control for overshoot compared to Cubic and smoother than Linear, making it effective for cases such as setting IK animation keys and creating animations in Godot.

**Linear:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f4e063b-602f-4ae6-97e2-e3f5ff5832ed

**Cubic:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6013d7df-fb39-4dd1-97e6-11af844c8066

**Makima:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/589cfc00-0408-4182-8f57-a39804698902

However, the performance cost is a bit of a concern in the current state of the higher dimension interpolation in Animation, so optimization or baking is recommended, as the same issue when using Cubic interpolation and Bezier tracks at runtime.

Contains fix for the old (mistaken/insufficient) docs.
